The real story in Indian e-commerce

Valmo: from 1.83% to 62% in three years.

Valmo is Meesho's proprietary logistics platform — a technology layer orchestrating multiple partners across a multi-stage network. Meesho holds zero inventory. Every percentage point shifted to Valmo means lower costs, better reliability, and eventually faster delivery — without a single dark store.

The forward-looking question

51–52%

of India's e-commerce will come from Tier 2+ cities by FY2030 — up from 44% today. That is Meesho's territory.

If Valmo reaches 80%+

Delivery compresses from 5 days to 2 days in Tier 2 cities — without dark store infrastructure. Unit economics improve dramatically on a ₹163 AOV order.

Meesho Grocery subsidiary

A separate entity building logistics for daily essentials — a signal that faster delivery for specific categories is already being tested. Not becoming Blinkit. Building something Blinkit cannot replicate.

A good case study doesn't just make the bull case

The risks are real.
They're just not quick commerce.

Risk 01

Seller Quality at Scale

513,000 fragmented sellers creates real challenges in product quality, delivery consistency, and compliance. One bad seller cohort erodes consumer trust at scale.

DRHP Risk 18 · Page 96
Risk 02

COD is Declining

88.71% (FY23) → 85.39% (FY24) → 76.95% (FY25) → 75.09% (Q1 FY26). As India digitises, Meesho's trust bridge with first-time users gradually weakens.

DRHP Page 87
Risk 03

The Monetisation Transition

Zero commissions is the moat. But approaching breakeven means needing more revenue per order — through ads, logistics fees, or financial services — without breaking seller trust.

DRHP Pages 34, 89, 93
07 / 08
Return rate: 7.57% FY25 (Page 104) — remarkably low for value commerce
Where I land

Meesho isn't competing with Blinkit. It's building the logistics infrastructure that will own Tier 2 India for the next decade. And Valmo is how they get there.

Blinkit's dark stores scale in Mumbai and Bengaluru. They do not scale in Jalgaon, Sikar, or Muzaffarpur. Valmo does. The winner of Indian e-commerce won't be the fastest company — it will be the one that cracked delivery at ₹163 AOV, at Tier 2 scale, profitably.
